content.user_title: Design Clear In-App Paywalls and Upgrade Flows
content.value_statement: Poorly timed paywalls and unclear upgrade messages can reduce conversions and damage user trust. This skill guides paywall copy, placement, subscription presentation, and experiments for product teams.
actual_capabilities: Draft screen copy for feature gates, usage limits, and trial expiration.
Recommend upgrade trigger points, prompt frequency limits, and dismissal behavior.
Outline paywall components, plan comparisons, pricing presentation, and upgrade paths.
Suggest A/B tests covering timing, layout, messaging, trials, and personalization.
Explain mobile subscription placement, renewal reminders, store review checks, and revenue per download.
Use available local product marketing context to tailor recommendations.
limitations: Provides recommendations and text examples, not a billing integration or deployed paywall.
Does not run experiments, collect analytics, or verify conversion improvements.
Store fees, platform rules, and cited benchmarks require independent verification against current sources.
Public pricing pages and broader pricing strategy are outside its primary scope.

use_cases.title: Improve a usage-limit upgrade screen
use_cases.description: Create clear upgrade copy, plan comparisons, and a dismissal option when free users reach a project limit.

use_cases.title: Plan a mobile subscription paywall
use_cases.description: Choose placement after a personalized result, present annual billing clearly, and estimate revenue per download using product assumptions.

use_cases.title: Prioritize paywall experiments
use_cases.description: Develop hypotheses for trigger timing, feature previews, and prompt frequency while tracking conversion, revenue, and post-upgrade churn.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic upgrade prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Our [product] limits free users to [limit]. Draft a paywall headline, benefit copy, upgrade button, and clear dismissal option.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: write a first usage-limit screen.

prompt_templates.title: Review a feature gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this paywall: [copy]. Users see it when attempting [feature]. Recommend a feature preview, clearer benefits, plan comparison, and dismissal behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve an existing feature gate.

prompt_templates.title: Design a mobile subscription flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Our [iOS or Android app] delivers [personalized result]. Recommend paywall placement, annual billing presentation, a trial reminder, and store review checks. State assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Build an experiment and economics plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [funnel metrics], [annual price], and [verified store fee], estimate revenue per download. Propose three prioritized paywall tests with hypotheses, metrics, and trust safeguards.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect experimentation with subscription economics.

output_examples.input: Free users can create three projects. Draft the upgrade screen shown when they attempt a fourth.
output: Headline: Create more projects with Pro.
Body: Your free plan includes three projects. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited projects.
Comparison: Free includes three projects; Pro includes unlimited projects. Show the confirmed price and billing period.
Actions: Upgrade to Pro, or return to your existing projects.
Timing: Show this screen at the fourth-project attempt and avoid repeated reminders after dismissal.

output_examples.input: A mobile app has a 30% trial start rate, 30% trial conversion, $30 annual price, and an assumed 15% store fee.
output: Estimated annual subscription revenue per download is $2.30 after the assumed store fee, rounded from $2.295.
Show the paywall after the first personalized result, with the full annual charge visible.
Schedule a trial-ending reminder and provide clear renewal terms.
Replace assumptions with observed cohorts and verified fees before setting acquisition spending.
This simplified estimate excludes refunds, taxes, operating costs, and later renewals.

best_practices: Provide product context, plan limits, and the exact moment users encounter the paywall.
Keep billing terms clear, dismissal visible, and reminder frequency respectful.
Validate recommendations with experiments and current platform rules rather than treating example figures as benchmarks.
anti_patterns: Hiding close controls, using misleading countdowns, or making plan selection confusing.
Showing upgrade prompts before users experience value or repeatedly after dismissal.
Treating suggested experiments, example conversion rates, or dated store fees as proven outcomes.

faq.question: Does this skill implement a working paywall?
faq.answer: No. It provides screen copy, flow recommendations, experiment ideas, and subscription calculations. Implementation and billing integration remain separate tasks.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Share your product, free and paid limits, upgrade trigger, user journey, pricing model, and available conversion metrics.

faq.question: Can it help with mobile subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. The mobile reference covers onboarding placement, annual plans, trials, renewal reminders, store checks, and revenue per download.

faq.question: Does it optimize public pricing pages?
faq.answer: Its primary scope is in-product upgrade moments. The source directs public pricing page work to a separate conversion optimization skill.

faq.question: Are conversion gains or fee estimates guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Test recommendations using your own data and verify current store fees, billing rules, and source benchmarks.

faq.question: Does it require product marketing context?
faq.answer: No. It uses a local product marketing context file when available and asks for missing task details.
